english.title: Disclose information in breach of section 41 confidentiality re identity of a person - UK Borders Act 2007
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) disclosed information relating to a person whose identity

(A)_[was specified in the disclosure]_
(B)_[could be deduced from the disclosure]_

in contravention of

(C)_[section 41]_
(D)_[section 41B]_

of the UK Borders Act 2007

english.notes:
(i) Section 42(2) of the UK Borders Act 2007 provides that the above offence does not apply to the disclosure of information about internal administrative arrangements of HMRC or the RCPO (whether relating to Commissioners, officers, members of the RCPO or others).
(ii) Section 42(3) of the UK Borders Act 2007 provides a defence for a person charged with the above offence to prove that he/she reasonably believed:-
(a) that the disclosure was lawful, or
(b) that the information had already and lawfully been made available to the public.
(iii) Section 41B of the Act inserted by section 20 of Borders, Citizenship and Immigration Act 2009.

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment and/or a fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2022; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 42(4) and(5) of the UK Borders Act 2007 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2022.
On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
